1 · Intro

When to use it.

These are the errors the HCM Academy courses warn about most. Each one sends wrong or missing data to payroll.

It is a draft. The list is not yet ranked by how often each error happens. Payroll will supply the errors it corrects most, and this course will be updated from that list on a schedule.

Use this whenYou want to check your own work against the errors that most often cause a late or wrong paycheck.

2 · Walk through

Ten errors to catch.

Check off each item as you read.

Watch-outs

  • Fixes after payroll runs become retro adjustments in a later payroll and may mean a late or incorrect paycheck.
  • If you find one of these after payroll has run, bring payroll the facts. Do not try to correct the pay yourself.
  • Open item: Payroll to supply the errors it corrects most often, with counts, so this list can be ranked and kept current.

Official documentation

Vendor documentation describes the standard process. Vanderbilt's setup, codes, and rules in this course take priority.

  • Oracle: Recalculate Payroll for Retroactive Changes (opens in a new tab)

3 · Knowledge check

Check your understanding.

Three questions. You get feedback on each answer. All three right completes the course.

Q1A new staff member's assignment status is Active no payroll. What happens on payday?

Q2You find a wrong effective date after payroll has run. What do you do?

Q3A supplement for a three-month interim role is left as Ongoing. What is the risk?

4 · Job aid

Keep it handy.

A one-page version of the steps and watch-outs. Print it or save it as a PDF.

HCM Academy job aid · Payroll & Timecards

Common pay errors and how to avoid them

Use when: You want to check your own work against the errors that most often cause a late or wrong paycheck. · System: Overview

  1. A paid person set to Active no payroll.
  2. A change still pending at the cutoff.
  3. The wrong effective date.
  4. Amount and Net mixed up on a one-time payment.
  5. A supplement that never ends.
  6. Hours changed without the salary, or the salary without the hours.
  7. A missing or unapproved time card.
  8. Terminate Employment used when the person keeps another job.
  9. Costing left as it was after a move.
  10. A wrong value on a position.

Watch-outs

  • Fixes after payroll runs become retro adjustments in a later payroll and may mean a late or incorrect paycheck.
  • If you find one of these after payroll has run, bring payroll the facts. Do not try to correct the pay yourself.
  • Open item: Payroll to supply the errors it corrects most often, with counts, so this list can be ranked and kept current.
